propositions: git commit --amend -F/-m replaces the entire commit message and drops the Change-Id trailer, causing Gerrit to stamp a new Change-Id and create a duplicate change instead of a new patchset
Git hooks cannot reliably distinguish an amend with -F from a fresh commit with -F, making hook-based solutions ineffective
A make amend-msg wrapper must preserve the existing Change-Id from HEAD while amending the message contents, following prior art from Go, OpenStack, Android, and Chromium
The wrapper must fail loudly and non-zero when HEAD carries no Change-Id, rather than silently creating a commit that will be stamped with a fresh one
AGENTS.md documentation must be updated to name make amend-msg as the path for rewritten commit messages and explicitly warn that --amend -m/-F drop the Change-Id and create duplicate Gerrit changes
